transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez, Ethan Park (Redwood); Daniel Reiss, Priya Nair, Marco Silva (Lyon)

Summary: quick intro then deep into SIG mapping and required evidence. A few places where words are fuzzy in transcription, e.g., "K-V cash" instead of KV cache, "Redwood Privatee" mis-typed.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Sofia from Redwood, I'll hand over to Ethan for the technical bits but quick agenda, go through your SIG, call out gaps, and agree next steps.
[00:08] Daniel: Thanks Sofia. Yep I can see agenda, our goal today is to understand what evidence you'll need for our procurement team, and also technical bits like SSO and where data sits. We're on a pretty tight timeline to get through vendor risk by end of month.
[00:18] Sofia: Got it. Timeline's helpful. Ethan, do you want to kick off with our SOC/ISO posture?
[00:23] Ethan: Sure. So high level, Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report covering security and availability, and we also have ISO 27001 in progress for the control set. Um the SOC 2 report is the typical thing procurement asks for, we'll share the redacted report. In the CAIQ mapping we usually link controls to the SOC sections.
[00:39] Priya: Do you have a date for the SOC 2 period covered? Our audit team needs dates to verify control overlap.
[00:44] Ethan: Yeah the latest report covers 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30. We can pop that into the sheet. There might be some redactions around customer names.
[00:52] Marco: When you say "share", is that via a portal or via e-mail? Procurement wants chain-of-custody, tamper-proof link ideally.
[00:58] Sofia: We typically upload to a secure S3 link with time-limited access and also support signing an NDA if needed. We'll provide a link and pointer in the CAIQ notes.
[01:07] Daniel: OK. On the CAIQ, we've got about 120 answered items already but procurement wants evidence for about 30 callouts, mostly around key management, audit logs retention, and encryption at rest.
[01:18] Ethan: Understood. For KMS we offer cloud KMS integrations — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS and Azure Key Vault for Private deployments, and for hosted we have managed encryption where keys are held by Redwood. If you need customer-managed keys, that's available on Dedicated or Private.
[01:37] Priya: That's good. Our default is customer-managed keys via AWS KMS. Does Redwood support envelope encryption and also rotation policies?
[01:44] Ethan: Yes. Envelope encryption supported; rotation policies can be defined on the KMS side. Small caveat: for hosted shared-tenancy we don't give you HSM-controlled a key with the same granting semantics as your AWS account — for full control you'd want Dedicated or Private where keys live in your tenancy or under your KMS.
[02:01] Daniel: So for shared hosted, Redwood manages keys but you can bring your own KMS in Private?
[02:06] Ethan: Exactly. Hosted = managed keys by Redwood with strong encryption; Dedicated/Private = BYOK (bring your own key) with customer KMS integration.
[02:13] Sofia: I'll add a note in the CAIQ answers clarifying which controls are only applicable to Dedicated/Private.
[02:18] Marco: Legal is also asking about data residency — where do requests get processed and stored?
[02:24] Ethan: For hosted we have region controls; data can be processed in region X, Y, Z (we'll include the exact regions). For Dedicated and Private, you control the region or on-prem location. We will document retention windows and log residency in the evidence.
[02:38] Priya: Audit logs — we need retention of 12 months for security events and 7 years for some compliance. Does Redwood's logging cover admin actions and API access logs?
[02:47] Ethan: Yes, we emit admin audit logs, token-level request logs, and model inference logs at a metadata level. Full raw request payloads are configurable — by default we don't store PII from requests; there's a config to disable request body retention for hosted. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3.
[03:07] Daniel: Can we get a schema of logs and log fields? Our security team wants to confirm fields like user_id, action, ip, timestamp, api_key_id.
[03:15] Ethan: Absolutely — we'll provide the log schema and sample events.
[03:18] Sofia: Quick question from procurement — what about pen tests and vulnerability scan evidence?
[03:22] Ethan: We run quarterly external vulnerability scans and annual penetration tests with a third-party vendor. We can provide summary reports and remediation timelines; full pen test reports can be shared under NDA.
[03:33] Priya: SSO integration — we use SAML 2.0, with SCIM for user provisioning. How mature is Redwood's SSO and RBAC?
[03:41] Ethan: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is role-based at the token and project level — you can map SAML groups to roles in our console. We also support session timeouts and IP allowlists for admin roles. The RBAC model has a set of built-in roles and you can create custom roles with permissions.
[03:58] Daniel: Any gotchas around session expiry and long-running inference jobs? We don't want jobs to fail if an admin token expires mid-job.
[04:05] Ethan: Good point — long running jobs use service account tokens rather than interactive SSO sessions. Interactive users get standard session lifetimes; for background workloads we recommend service accounts with scoped tokens and audit logging for actions.
[04:18] Marco: Does audit capture service account actions the same as user actions?
[04:22] Ethan: Yes; service account actions are logged with the account id and associated project.
[04:26] Priya: For CAIQ, some of the questions are very granular — for example about cryptographic algorithm suites. Do you provide specifics like AES256-GCM, RSA-2048 for certs, TLS versions?
[04:36] Ethan: Yes we'll include algorithm details and TLS versions (we currently require TLS 1.2+). For disk encryption we use AES-256-GCM where supported.
[04:44] Daniel: On the SIG evidence list, procurement flagged "availability SLAs" and asked if you have redundancy across AZs and backup frequency.
[04:52] Ethan: For Hosted we have multi-AZ deployments with active-active routing for serving. Backups occur nightly and we have point-in-time recovery for configs; RTO/RPO depends on the deployment type, which we'll list in the evidence doc.
[05:05] Sofia: I'll make sure the SLA matrix is attached. Also some procurement folks will want a contact for escalation.
[05:11] Marco: Please include an on-call escalation process and runbook overview.
[05:15] Ethan: We can include our incident response summary and an on-call escalation flow — the detailed runbook we'll share under NDA if needed.
[05:24] Daniel: A few specific SIG questions — one is about residual data on GPUs / inference caches, like KV cache. Does Redwood scrub KV cache between tenants?
[05:33] Ethan: Yes. We scrub KV cache between model sessions and have strict memory isolation for tenants. There was a note in the call: transcription may show "K-V cash" — but functionally it's the KV cache. We'll provide tech docs on memory isolation.
[05:47] Priya: Great. A question on encryption for embeddings — some vendors store embeddings and claim they're irreversible, we have to treat them as potential sensitive derivatives. What's Redwood's approach?
[05:57] Ethan: We treat embeddings as data; retention and storage follow the same policies as request bodies. For hosted, embeddings can be stored if configured for caching; otherwise set the cache to zero retention. For Dedicated/Private, storage is under customer control and encryption is via customer keys if BYOK.
[06:13] Marco: On the CAIQ sheet you'll see we left a few items as "control implemented but evidence pending". Is there a way you can pre-fill common answers to speed review?
[06:22] Sofia: Yes, we usually pre-fill about 70% of the CAIQ with standard answers and suggest attachments for evidence. We'll send the spreadsheet with comments.
[06:29] Daniel: For secure evidence transfer, procurement uses an internal vault that needs checksums. Do you provide checksums on downloads?
[06:35] Ethan: We can provide SHA256 checksums on artifacts we share.
[06:39] Priya: Anything about third-party subprocessors? Procurement wants a list of subprocessors and subcontractors and their locations.
[06:46] Ethan: We maintain a subprocessors list and can provide a redacted view in the evidence pack; full disclosure is also possible under an NDA for the procurement review.
[06:56] Marco: One more procurement Q — pricing impact if we require Private deployment + BYOK for keys and specific region residency?
[07:04] Sofia: That will typically be a dedicated pricing line — Dedicated/Private incurs platform and infra fees. We'll put a stub pricing note in the follow-up, but detailed commercial terms will go through your procurement rep and our sales ops.
[07:16] Daniel: For the SSO demo next week, can you show group mapping and SCIM provisioning end-to-end? That would help our IAM team.
[07:23] Ethan: Yep, we can do a 30-min technical demo with SCIM provisioning and a quick RBAC mapping example. We'll ask you to provide a test IdP or we can provide a sample OneLogin/Okta instance for the demo.
[07:36] Priya: We'll prefer to use our Okta test tenant, I'll coordinate that.
[07:41] Sofia: Great. Now just to cover some SIG specifics — control CA-2 style questions around configuration management and vulnerability remediation windows. We typically state a 30 day remediation SLG for medium/high-criticality items?
[07:55] Ethan: Typically critical issues are triaged immediately and patched per security response policies. Medium/low have a 30/90 day window respectively; we'll put that in the CAIQ notes.
[08:08] Marco: Is there an ISO certificate in flight? Procurement asks if ISO 27001 will be available by Q1 next year.
[08:14] Ethan: We're in the final stages of certification; target is end of Q1 2027. We'll update you if the timeline shifts.
[08:22] Daniel: On data residency compliance in EMEA, can you support EU-only processing and storage?
[08:28] Ethan: Yes for Dedicated/Private we can ensure EU-only region hosting. For hosted, we have EU region endpoints; we'll document where data is physically stored and the flows in the evidence pack.
[08:40] Priya: A small technical nit — are model weights stored in encrypted form at rest? Some vendor forms ask explicitly.
[08:46] Ethan: We store model artifacts encrypted at rest using AES-256; we'll include the encryption details in the evidence.
[08:53] Marco: For audit requests, how quickly can you produce logs for a forensic investigation?
[08:58] Ethan: We can produce logs within 72 hours for a standard request; for expedited/legal requests we have SLAs that require escalation and may vary. We'll document our log retrieval process and typical timelines.
[09:11] Daniel: There are also questions about pen test remediation verification — do you provide attestation that the fixes were applied?
[09:18] Ethan: We'll provide remediation timelines, patching proofs, and for critical items we can provide verification snapshots or recompliance test results.
[09:28] Sofia: Back to the CAIQ — we'll send you a pre-filled spreadsheet and a separate evidence checklist highlighting the 30 items your procurement flagged. In that checklist we'll label items: evidence attached, evidence pending, requires configuration, or not applicable.
[09:44] Priya: That sounds ideal. For SSO metadata, what do you need from us ahead of the demo?
[09:49] Ethan: SAML metadata XML or Okta/OneLogin connection details and a test user with group memberships to show mapping. Also SCIM service credentials if you want provisioning.
[09:58] Priya: I'll get that to you by Monday.
[10:00] Marco: Anything else we should expect in the evidence pack? We need to see control owners and contact info for escalation.
[10:07] Sofia: Yes, we'll attach control owner names and an escalation contact list for security and procurement.
[10:12] Daniel: Can you also call out controls that are not applicable because of architecture decisions? Procurement wants justification text for N/A answers.
[10:19] Ethan: We'll add short rationales for N/A items in the CAIQ comments.
[10:24] Marco: Regarding backups — do you provide encrypted backups and a key rotation schedule?
[10:29] Ethan: Backups are encrypted; key rotation frequency is documented and we can provide the schedule and procedures.
[10:35] Priya: About the log forwarding — is there a streaming option to our SIEM? Or do you only provide batch exports?
[10:41] Ethan: Both. We can stream events via secure syslog or push to S3 buckets. For low-latency monitoring we recommend streaming.
[10:50] Daniel: A small procurement ask: can you include a short paragraph on insurance / cyber coverage limits?
[10:56] Sofia: Yes, we can include our cyber insurance summary in the evidence pack.
[11:01] Marco: On subprocessors, are there any that are outside EU/US? Procurement is worried about APAC-based subprocessors.
[11:08] Ethan: We have some partners in APAC for edge routing and support but core data processing is in the regions we declared; we'll provide a redacted subprocessors list with locations. Full list under NDA.
[11:21] Priya: For isolation at the GPU level — you mentioned memory isolation. Is multi-tenant inference done on separate GPUs or partitioned?
[11:29] Ethan: Several approaches — for some instance types we use hardware partitioning and for others we schedule single-tenant GPU instances depending on model size and tenancy. We'll detail which models and sizes use which strategy in the evidence docs.
[11:44] Daniel: Great. Anything else from the Redwood side?
[11:47] Ethan: We'll also include a short tech note on KV cache behavior and how to disable caching per request.
[11:53] Sofia: OK wrapping up. Quick recap of next steps: Redwood sends SOC2 report, CAIQ prefilled spreadsheet with comments, log schema, KMS/keys summary, subprocessors list (redacted) and an evidence checklist by 2026-12-15. Lyon to send SIG baseline and test Okta metadata by 2026-12-17. Schedule SSO/RBAC demo for week of 2026-12-21.
[12:13] Daniel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:16] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.
[12:18] Sofia: Thanks all. Bye.

Post-call notes (manual):
- There are a few spots where Fireflies auto-transcription mis-heard technical terms; when we send the official evidence pack ensure the technical docs use exact terminology (KMS, KV cache, SAML metadata).
- Procurement cares about delivery method and checksums for evidence. Include SHA256 on each artifact.
- Several items will require NDA for full disclosure (pen test full reports, full subprocessors list).

End of transcript.
